title: async-batcher-shim-and-kvcache-health-probes
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: The continuous batcher and the legacy executor are joined by a thin compatibility layer that creates jitter under certain traffic patterns and makes kvcache health hard to reason about. We see intermittent tail latency regressions (~95th-99th spikes) during small bursts and cold-starts. The existing kvcache lacks explicit liveness signals and the prefetch heuristics are embedded in multiple places, making it hard to tune safely.

Goal: Introduce an async batcher shim that standardizes enqueue/dequeue semantics for both the coroutine-based executor and the older threaded executor, and add explicit kvcache health probes + a lightweight refresh heuristic. This reduces handoffs, simplifies backpressure reasoning, and gives the autoscaler and orchestrator clearer signals to avoid over-eviction or over-prefetching.

Acceptance criteria:
- New shim passes unit and e2e tests and is toggleable via runtime flag (--async-batcher-shim).
- 95th and 99th percentile latency for small-burst microbench (10qps -> 200qps spike) reduced by >=15% vs baseline.
- KV cache exposes a /health endpoint returning: hit_rate_1m, stale_evictions, refresh_queue_depth, last_refresh_timestamp. Health is emitted to console tracing and to the tenant telemetry pipeline.
- A refresh heuristic is implemented: if hit_rate_1m < 0.6 and refresh_queue_depth < 50, schedule opportunistic refresh for top-200 session keys in LRU window.
- Rollback plan documented and tested in staging.

Non-goals: full replacement of batcher runtime architecture or changing allocator strategy in this ticket. Those are follow-ups.

Plan (phases):
1) Prototype shim as library module with a minimal adapter layer to existing enqueue API (2d).
2) Implement kvcache probe hooks and health endpoint; wire to telemetry (3d).
3) Integrate refresh heuristic and add conservative circuit breaker to avoid thundering refreshes (2d).
4) Canary on dedicated cluster with synthetic burst tests and gradual traffic ramp (4d).
5) Address perf regressions and finalize runtime flag as GA (1–2d).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: refresh heuristic could amplify load if refreshes miss. Mitigation: circuit breaker + per-tenant rate limit + conservative defaults.
- Risk: shim introduces contention on shared queue structures. Mitigation: use lock-free MPSC ring for hot path; bench before canary.

Docs and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Async+Batcher+Shim
- Benchmark dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/staging/batcher_latency?panel=5
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124
comments: 2026-02-21 — Asha Patel: Spiked prototype in a branch. Initial approach uses a small MPSC ring and a coroutine-driven consumer. End-to-end test shows reduced jitter in synthetic microbench but increased CPU by ~3% in baseline load. Filed follow-up notes in design doc.

2026-02-25 — Marco Delgado: Reviewed prototype. Agreed to move forward but replace naive mutex-backed queue with lock-free ring to reduce CPU. Added estimate to candidate work: 5 points. Assigned to Marco for implementation.

2026-03-01 — Priya Shah (SRE): Requested explicit health metrics exposed by kvcache before canary. Listed required fields and retention. Linked Grafana alert thresholds in SRE playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/KVCache+Alerts

2026-03-07 — Marco Delgado: Implemented health endpoint and refresh heuristic. Hooked health into observable pipeline; dashboard shows refresh_queue_depth metric. Observed a regression in memory spikes during initial runs; adding per-tenant cap and circuit breaker as discussed.

2026-03-12 — Engineering Review: Ran staged canary on dedicated-01 for 48h. Latency: p95 improved by 18%, p99 improved by 12% in 10->200 qps spike test. Noted ~4% CPU uplift sustained on nodes. Decision: proceed with controlled rollout to 10% of runtime-1.30 traffic, monitor for two full business cycles. Follow-up ticket to optimize memory churn (ENG-101011).
